claim: DEGGS is the per-PLAYER egg-hit counter that drives the EGGVAL ladder: `DEGGS RMB 2` is declared inside the `* DECISION BLOCK *` (ORG $0, JOUSTRV4.SRC:101-113), so it is decision-area state, NOT egg state. This is why jt8-4 homes the count on the player process and not on EggState.hitCount. (JOUSTRV4.SRC:113).
PLYEGG is the player-vs-egg collision entry point — 'COLISION DETECT WITH THE EGG'. The catch pass in demo.ts collisionPass is this routine. (JOUSTRV4.SRC:3009).

source.verbatim: PLYEGG	EQU	*		COLISION DETECT WITH THE EGG

claim: The player/egg collision collects the egg's score by calling EGGSCR — the collision IS the scoring trigger; there is no separate pickup step. (JOUSTRV4.SRC:3021).

source.verbatim: JSR	EGGSCR		COLLECT THE EGGS SCORE VALUE

claim: EGGSCR finds the incrementing ladder count through the CATCHING PLAYER's decision area: LDY PDECSN,U, where U is documented at :3025-3026 as "THE PLAYER'S (VICTOR) WORKSPACE THAT HIT THE EGG" (X is the egg's). The counter is reached via U, never via X. (JOUSTRV4.SRC:3033).

source.verbatim: LDY	PDECSN,U	FIND INCREMENTING SCORE VALUE FOR EGG

claim: The decision area's egg counter is DEGGS: LDY DEGGS,Y loads the pointer to the count that indexes EGGVAL, after Y was set to the catching player's PDECSN. (JOUSTRV4.SRC:3037).

EGGSMN writes the bumped (and capped) count BACK to the counter: STB ,Y. This write-back is what makes the ladder CLIMB across successive catches WITHIN one life — EGGSCR itself never resets it. That is a fact about EGGSCR and not about the counter's lifetime: the reset boundaries live in three other places (a new game :907/:912, EVERY wave start WNRM :1979-1980, and the player's own death-wish routine DEATH1/DEATH2 :4669/:4675 — see JT86-002..007). (JOUSTRV4.SRC:3053).

On collecting an egg whose rider had an inbound remount bird (PDIST,X non-zero, :3078), the bird is sent away: LDD #AUTOFF — 'THE BIRD SHOULD GO OFF SCREEN'. Our port matures a settled wave egg straight into the remount enemy, so egg and inbound bird never coexist; the reachable analogue is that a caught egg is removed before the hatch matures it. (JOUSTRV4.SRC:3086).

source.verbatim: LDD	#AUTOFF		THE BIRD SHOULD GO OFF SCREEN

claim: AUTOFF is written into the inbound bird's joystick-program pointer: STD PJOY,Y — the bird keeps flying but under the auto-off-screen program. (JOUSTRV4.SRC:3087).

A collected egg stops participating in collisions: LDA PID,X — 'NO LONGER COLIDE WITH EGG'. The ROM keeps the process alive to float the score value (EGGWAK re-points PPC at EGGHIT, :3088-3091); jt8-4 removes the process instead, which is the honest subset — collected once, never twice. (JOUSTRV4.SRC:3092).

source.verbatim: LDA	PID,X		NO LONGER COLIDE WITH EGG

claim: The collide bit is masked off with ANDA #$7F — clearing PID bit 7 ($80), the same collision-enable bit jt2-6's materialisation window toggles. JOUSTRV4.SRC is bare-decimal with $ hex, so $7F is 127. (JOUSTRV4.SRC:3093).
